issues.legal_issue: A preliminary notification issued under a repealed municipal law may support a valid inclusion under the successor law when the successor law preserves prior administrative actions.
material_facts: The government declared its intention to include two villages within the municipality under the former municipal law.
After the successor municipal law came into force, the government issued a final notification including the villages under that law.
The successor law provided that qualifying actions taken under the former law were to be treated as actions taken under the successor law.
issues.conclusion: The inclusion of the villages within the municipality was valid.
issues.legal_principle: Clause 13 of Schedule IX, read with clause 1 of the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965, deemed prior actions under the repealed District Municipalities Act, 1920 to have been taken under the successor Act unless inconsistent with it. The preliminary notification was therefore treated as having been issued under section 3(1)(b) of the successor Act.

predicates.municipal_boundary_inclusion_case: The proceeding concerns whether a local area was validly included within a municipality.
predicates.government_started_inclusion_under_prior: The government began the process of including a local area under an earlier municipal regime before a successor regime took effect.
predicates.successor_framework_preserved_prior_admi: The successor framework treated qualifying administrative steps taken under the earlier regime as steps taken under the successor regime.

issues.definition: When a boundary-inclusion proceeding involves an inclusion process begun under an earlier regime and the successor framework preserved prior administrative steps, the inclusion is valid.

issues.legal_issue: A transitional provision continuing existing municipal taxes does not authorize a tax in a newly included area where that tax was not being levied there when the successor law took effect.
material_facts: The properties at issue were in villages that were outside the municipality before their inclusion.
The property owners had paid taxes to the village panchayat, but no municipal property tax was being levied on their properties when the successor municipal law took effect in the villages.
The municipality demanded property tax for the period beginning when the villages were included, relying on the transitional provision for continuing existing taxes.
issues.conclusion: The transitional provision did not authorize the municipality to levy property tax on the newly included properties for that earlier period.
issues.legal_principle: Clause 12 of Schedule IX of the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965, was a transitional provision authorizing continuation of taxes lawfully being levied at the commencement of the Act, provided they could lawfully be levied under the Act. It did not authorize a tax on property in an area where that tax was not then being levied.

rule.if: municipal_tax_continuation_case and property_area_newly_added and not tax_being_levied_in_area_at_transition

predicates.municipal_tax_continuation_case: The proceeding concerns whether a municipality may continue a tax under a transitional arrangement.
predicates.property_area_newly_added: The property subject to the proposed tax is in an area newly brought within the municipality.
predicates.tax_being_levied_in_area_at_transition: A municipal council was levying the relevant tax on the property in that area when the successor municipal regime took effect.

issues.definition: When a continuation proceeding concerns property in a newly added area where the relevant tax was not being levied at the transition, continuation of that tax is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: A municipality imposing property tax for the first time on a newly included area must follow the required advance notice and objection procedure for that area, even if it already levies the same tax elsewhere.
material_facts: The municipality had long levied property tax on properties within its pre-existing boundaries.
The newly included villages had been outside those boundaries and their residents had not been assessed to municipal property tax.
The council later followed an objection process and resolved to levy property tax prospectively, but demanded tax for an earlier period without following that process for the earlier levy.
issues.conclusion: The levy for the period before the required first-time tax procedure was followed was without authority of law and illegal.
issues.legal_principle: Section 81(1)(a) of the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965, required a council to levy property tax by resolution. Under the first proviso to section 81(2), before imposing a tax for the first time, the council had to publish notice, invite objections, and consider objections received within the stipulated time. Section 83, which required publication of a notification specifying the rate and commencement of a first-time tax, was expressly subject to section 81. A tax was being imposed for the first time as to the newly included area, notwithstanding its prior levy elsewhere.

predicates.municipal_property_tax_case: The proceeding concerns a municipal council's imposition of property tax.
predicates.council_imposed_tax_in_new_area: A municipal council imposed property tax on properties in an area newly brought within the municipality.
predicates.council_followed_first_time_tax_objectio: Before imposing the tax in the area, the council published notice, invited objections, and considered objections received within the specified time.

issues.definition: When a property-tax proceeding concerns a tax imposed in a newly added area without the first-time tax objection process, the levy before that process is unlawful.

issues.legal_issue: An opportunity to object to the inclusion of an area within a municipality is not an opportunity to object to a later property tax imposed on that area.
material_facts: The government published a notification stating its intention to include the villages within the municipality.
Residents could object to matters contained in that notification, which concerned the proposed inclusion of the villages.
The municipality later sought to impose property tax on the newly included area without providing the separate tax-objection process for the period in dispute.
issues.conclusion: The inclusion notification did not replace the required opportunity to object to the imposition of property tax.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3(2) and 3(3) of the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965, allowed objections to the proposed inclusion of an area. Those objections concerned the contents of the inclusion notification, not a proposed tax. A tax question arose after the final inclusion notification, and a tax resolution then had to comply with section 81, including its first-time tax objection procedure.

predicates.municipal_tax_objection_case: The proceeding concerns whether residents had a proper opportunity to object to a municipal tax.
predicates.residents_could_object_only_to_area_incl: Residents were invited to object to a proposal to add their area to a municipality, rather than to a proposal to impose a tax there.
predicates.tax_objection_process_not_separately_pro: The municipality did not separately invite and consider objections to the proposed tax.

issues.definition: When residents could object only to the inclusion of their area and no separate tax-objection process was provided, the inclusion objection opportunity does not satisfy the tax objection requirement.

issues.legal_issue: Including an area within a municipality does not automatically extend an existing municipal tax or an earlier tax resolution to that area.
material_facts: The government issued a final notification including the villages within the municipality.
The municipality had previously levied property tax in its existing areas but had not imposed it in the newly included villages.
The council later adopted a resolution to impose property tax in the newly included area after considering objections, but demanded tax for an earlier period.
issues.conclusion: The inclusion of the villages did not automatically extend the existing tax or prior tax resolutions to them; the municipality had to follow the statutory tax-imposition procedure for the new area.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(4) of the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965, brought the Act's provisions into force in an included area, including sections 81 and 83. It did not extend earlier tax resolutions automatically to that area. The tax-imposition procedures in sections 81 and 83 had to be followed. The Court explained Atlas Cycle Industries Ltd. v. State of Haryana, which likewise held that inclusion of an area did not by itself authorize a tax levy without the required tax procedure.

predicates.municipal_tax_extension_case: The proceeding concerns whether an existing municipal tax or resolution extends to a newly added area.
predicates.area_added_to_municipality: The government included a local area within an existing municipality.
predicates.tax_resolution_predated_area_inclusion: The council adopted the relevant tax resolution before the local area was included in the municipality.

issues.definition: When an area is added to a municipality after a tax resolution was adopted, the prior tax resolution does not automatically apply to that new area.
